decision: Every change carries a record made by ocoeco (a changes table in the shared language), the commit message is rendered from it, and ocoeco release consumes the records to set the version, write release notes tied to milestones and backlog, and tag - taking over from release-please and release-plz. The guarantee is at the boundaries that cannot be skipped: land refuses a change with no record, and a CI check on every pull request does the same; a local hook only points the way. Local commits stay free; the record is per change. Refined the same day by 2026-11-11-glimpses: the record is the glimpse, made while the work is fresh; a change is the glimpses it carries.
why: The author: data about work goes stale because nothing guarantees it is produced; release tooling writes prose nobody consumes, while ocoeco already knows tasks, goals, decisions and effort. 48% of recent landings produced any data.
rejected: Records only in commit messages (lost to squash merges, readable only through git); refusing every local commit with hooks (they fight rebase and amend, are bypassed with --no-verify, and the bypass becomes routine); adopting changesets or Knope as they are (a bump and a summary, tied to nothing else); keeping release-please (prose that drives nothing).

decision: ocoeco check reads a project's essence as advice and never fails on a gap.
why: A gap is the truth about a project, not an error in its data.
rejected: Failing the check until every step is served.

decision: Code is changed by structure: whole items replaced with ast-grep, matched by their signature; logic kept outside macros where tools and readers see it; new views and tools added as new files; every edit verified before anything lands.
why: Patching source by matching text was the heaviest manual work (19 times) and the cause of most failed runs, one of which landed a commit that changed nothing.
rejected: Text patches with better anchors; Comby (language-agnostic, less exact for Rust); writing our own rewriter.

decision: Hand-work saturation is measured in effort - minutes weighted by load on Borg's CR10 scale - as well as count; there is no deliberate status: looking, listening and deciding are counted and automatable like the rest.
why: The author's 30 kg box: ten seconds, yet draining. And tests must judge sound and pictures themselves, with no person judging mid-run (jidoka).
rejected: Count alone; NASA-TLX's six ratings on every bump (too heavy); exempting judgment from automation.

decision: The record of work is the glimpse, made through ocoeco at any moment while the work is fresh; ocoeco supplies most of it (what ocoeco note wrote since the last glimpse, the backlog items and milestones they serve, the effort), and the person or agent types a line. ocoeco commit renders a commit from the glimpses not yet committed, with a trailer per glimpse; ocoeco release consumes the glimpses of what has landed. Git depends on ocoeco, never the reverse: a glimpse needs no git.
why: The author: capture data where it is fresh, while the work is remembered, not sorted out afterwards; and git operations depend on ocoeco, not ocoeco on git. This refines 2026-11-11-changes-are-records, whose record was tied to a change.
rejected: One record per change, written at commit time (later than the work, and tied to git); records only in commit messages; hooks refusing every local commit.

decision: Hand-work becomes part of ocoeco's language: a handwork table of atomic actions with counts, recorded by ocoeco hand (match, bump, or ask), shown by the observatory as hand-work worth a tool.
why: Proposed by the author. A board task is many steps and never repeats; atomic actions do. The wording is kept from drifting by the tool, as the vocabulary keeps words from drifting.
rejected: Logging whole tasks (they never repeat); free-text notes in the session log (they cannot be counted); bumping on any resemblance without asking (silent merging of different actions).

decision: ocoeco check names every table a repository keeps beside its exported ones but does not export.
why: A device lab's whole backlog and a tool's decisions and log went unseen by the observatory for days; ocoeco note found it by refusing.
rejected: Exporting every file automatically - some are kept for a project's own use.

decision: The shared language is language.toml, a tad declaration; ocoeco note checks each row it writes with tad's check_row; the shapes kept as Rust constants are gone.
why: One way to declare and check tables across the commons: tad's, readable by people and by any tool. A test proved the file said exactly what the constants said before they were removed; ocoeco's own tests pass unchanged.
rejected: Rewriting every project's tables in tad's canonical form now (churn in 22 projects, no reader gains); keeping the shapes in Rust (a second declaration language).

decision: Hand-work is called manual work everywhere - the table manual_work, the command ocoeco manual, land --manual; every record and bump appends a timed event to manual_events.
why: The author: manual work is the plain word, and with the time kept it can be set beside commits and releases. A command named manual could be read as documentation; the vocabulary defines it, and ocoeco has no documentation command to collide with.
rejected: hand-work (less plain); ocoeco did (the person does, not the tool); inventing times for the history recorded before.

decision: Rows are recorded with ocoeco note, not hand-written per job.
why: Every job wrote its own script to patch JSON: the same handwork again and again, each a chance to break a table. On its first use the tool found that ocoeco itself exported no decisions.
rejected: A per-job script; a general JSON editor that knows nothing of the format.

decision: ocoeco manual without an action opens a list in the terminal (ratatui): type to narrow, arrows, Enter, the usual minutes and load offered.
why: Asked by the author: typing an action again is a chore and splits the ledger into near-duplicates.
rejected: A web form (not TTY-first); fuzzy matching on typed text alone (it guesses).

decision: Research joins the language as its own table (question, found, sources, date); decisions cite it and name the steps they are about; the observatory badges each step with its decisions.
why: Asked by the author: research should back decisions visibly, beside the milestones and progress they concern, and looking around should be a practice for agents and humans alike.
rejected: Sources alone (a list of works says nothing of the question asked); a separate research page with no link to steps.

decision: Any row may be researched rather than live: it cites a research entry and is drawn outlined, with its age and a link; research gains versions (topic, date, supersedes), a refresh horizon, and a place in the attention view when it goes stale.
why: Asked by the author, to fill the picture honestly with what others achieved.
rejected: Copying outside claims in as if measured; overwriting research on refresh; marking live data (live is the default).

decision: Vocabulary becomes part of ocoeco's language: a vocabulary table (term, means, not, see), the shared words defined by ocoeco itself, a project's own words beside them, translated like everything else, and shown in views.
why: Asked for by the author, so the work can be spoken about clearly; concepts and vocabulary answer different questions.
rejected: Folding definitions into the concepts table; a glossary written by the observatory about projects.

decision: Where the whole is weakest right now is where attention goes.
why: What should be looked at next, read from every project - not what is loudest.
rejected: triage (medical jargon); focus; priorities (a ranking someone sets)

decision: An idea a project rests on, with why it matters, is a concept.
why: Distinct from idea (why the project exists) and from vocabulary (what a word means).
rejected: principle (a rule to follow, a narrower thing); belief

decision: A shared process that projects call, not copy, is a conveyor.
why: A conveyor carries any load the same way; you put work on it, you do not build your own.
rejected: pipeline (CI jargon, and one run); template (copied, the opposite)

decision: A lens chosen to stand in the observatory's navigation is curated.
why: Says chosen with care, and nothing more; any lens is still found without it.
rejected: featured, pinned (web jargon); official (claims an authority it does not have)

decision: An owned fork pinned upstream and changed only as patches meant to go home is a cutting.
why: Rhizoid's gardening word: a cutting is a living piece of the parent plant, grown in your soil.
rejected: fork (suggests drifting apart); vendored copy (a frozen copy, nothing goes home)

decision: A choice taken, with why and what was rejected, is a decision.
why: The plain word; the rejected options are what make it worth keeping.
rejected: ADR (an acronym a reader must be taught); choice (says nothing of the alternatives)

decision: Minutes weighted by load are effort.
why: Effort is the plain word for time and strain together - the 30 kg box.
rejected: cost (money); toil score (jargon); workload (NASA-TLX's wider measure)

decision: A project's whole chain on one page is its essence.
why: Essence is what a thing most truly is; the page shows why, what, how and now at once.
rejected: overview, summary (say less, not more); dashboard (numbers, no reasons); at a glance

decision: The daily job that writes down what a project's work produced is its gatherer.
why: One metaphor, kept whole: gatherers in each field, the harvest brought in by the observatory.
rejected: collector (monitoring jargon); logger; recorder (plain, but breaks the metaphor)

decision: The observatory's reading of every marked project is the harvest.
why: It brings in what the gatherers gathered; the pair is easy to keep in mind.
rejected: crawl, scrape (say how, not what); sync; import

decision: The three stretches of a path are horizons.
why: Horizons are near and far at once - working, perfection and ongoing perfection are all in view together.
rejected: phase, stage (imply one ends before the next begins); level (sounds like a score)

decision: Why a project exists, told for anyone, is its idea.
why: The everyday word; a reader knows what an idea is without being taught.
rejected: vision, mission (corporate jargon); pitch (selling); purpose (narrower)

decision: A grand view of a family of projects, declared as a small file, is a lens.
why: You look through a lens; many lenses can look at the same commons, and anyone may make one.
rejected: view (every page is a view - two meanings); dashboard; portal

decision: How draining an action was this time is its load.
why: Short and physical, as in carrying a load; one number from Borg's CR10.
rejected: exertion (formal); fatigue (an aftermath, not the act); difficulty

decision: The file by which a repository joins the commons is a mark.
why: Short and plain: a mark is something you put on a thing to say what it belongs to.
rejected: manifest (a package's description elsewhere - two meanings); badge (a picture); tag (GitHub topics are only half of it)

decision: A step on a path is a milestone, reached only when its evidence exists.
why: The word readers know; the vocabulary adds only the rule that evidence reaches it, not a date.
rejected: step (too small to name a stretch of work); goal (aims, not proves); checkpoint

decision: The mirror that reads and draws the commons is the observatory.
why: One watches from an observatory and changes nothing: the mirror, not the control centre.
rejected: dashboard, portal, hub (suggest control)

decision: The commons' language and machinery keep their own name, ocoeco.
why: A proper name, chosen by the author: the observatory's ecosystem - the blood and heart.
rejected: a descriptive name (it is the name of a thing, not a description)

decision: What a project must reach is its path.
why: A path is walked step by step and says nothing of dates - exactly a list of milestones with their evidence.
rejected: roadmap (promises dates, a second meaning we do not want); plan; route

decision: A repository with a mark is a project.
why: The plain word everyone already uses; one repository, one project, one mark.
rejected: repository (says where, not what); module; component

decision: The look around before acting is research.
why: The everyday word for looking into something before deciding.
rejected: prior art (the sources, not the looking); investigation; due diligence (legal)

decision: Manual work done often or heavily enough to ask for a tool is saturated.
why: The author's own word; it says full - nothing more should be carried by hand.
rejected: overdue (blames); hot spot (jargon)

decision: A work a project stands on is a source.
why: The word readers know from any citation.
rejected: reference (also means a pointer); citation (the act, not the work)

decision: The words a project speaks and exactly what they mean are its vocabulary.
why: A vocabulary is a language spoken - the ubiquitous language of domain-driven design - not a list kept at the back.
rejected: glossary (a list at the back of a book); dictionary; terminology (formal)

decision: What actually happens is work: the backlog, the log, what the gatherers record.
why: Plain, and set against the plan; the Essence page asks of it: what is happening now.
rejected: activity (only commits); progress (a judgment, not a record)

decision: How the steps are delivered and proven are its workings, as in the workings of a clock; a single entry is called by its kind.
why: Workings is everyday English for the parts that make something work. Working as a singular noun is unusual and was the weakest word in the language.
rejected: working (unusual as a noun); means (plain, but it would collide with the vocabulary's own means field - one word, two meanings); mechanism (sounds like code only); instrument

decision: Words are chosen like decisions: a vocabulary entry names the decision that chose it, the decision records the words rejected and cites research; every vocabulary is reviewed this way.
why: Asked by the author: wording is part of perfection. A word is how everyone after us will think about the thing.
rejected: Definitions without reasons; leaving the words as they first came.

decision: A lens's focus is declared as data in its file: parts, each a query over the lens's gathered tables and one line laying out an answer ({name} is that answer's value; {count} in a heading; {today} supplied by the computer). ocoeco focus LENS gathers the lens's tables from this place, or from every place under a root - each row with its star - and runs the parts through tad's SQL engine. The work lens's focus replaces the hand-written board: on every star's main it printed the same 12 lines, byte for byte.
why: The same data, brought into focus (2026-11-12-a-lens-focuses), and proven equal before replacing, as tad's Rust version was. How it reads is now data: changing a word is editing the lens, not the program.
rejected: A language of its own for layout (one line per answer is enough to equal the board; more is added when a lens needs it, not before); formatting in Rust (the hand-written view lenses exist to end); replacing the board before the focus equalled it.

decision: A lens may add meaning to what it brings into focus; only a surface adds looks. The first meaning: a line that is a measure of a whole (measure = COLUMN, of = N in a focus part) - shown by each surface in its own way: a native meter on the page, a bar of ten cells on text, Markdown and the terminal. The purpose lens says its milestones are measures of nine. A lens placed over other lenses - a colour lens, in the author's words - fits the same way: it adds what its colour means, never the colour. Later the same day the author set the colour lens aside (backlog a-lens-over-lenses, parked): the meaning is already carried by the lens that holds the data; nothing is built toward a lens whose work is beauty.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: we will be able to add more lenses, the naming again discovered naturally - a colour lens, a lens that uses other lenses to make what they already focus more beautiful or convenient, like the infographics the earlier page had. Astronomy does this with colour filters: the same light, through a filter, shows what the plain view leaves flat. The inset that had leaked from the text surface into every lens was removed the same day; beauty kept in a lens would bring layout back. A readiness bar is not decoration: it says this is a quantity of a whole. Proven: six other lenses print byte for byte what they printed, and every lens comes into focus over every star.
rejected: Looks in a lens - colours, bars, spacing (a lens would know its surfaces again); an infographic as a surface of its own for one lens (it would not just work for the next lens with a measure); a word for the lens-over-lenses chosen before one is built (filter is the candidate, to be found in the making).

decision: The second face of a lens is its focus, not its showing; ocoeco's acts are glimpse, observe and focus. A lens lets data through and brings it into focus; what is seen is on the fulldome. Shine names no act: it is what a star does by working.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: a lens propagates light, by itself it shows nothing, and showing is a word from another domain. Optics defines a lens by exactly this - it transmits light and brings it to a focus (research the-word-focus). The word also parts two things that showing had run together: the lens that orders, and the fulldome where it is seen.
rejected: show and showing; render; resolve; image; project and projection; reveal (each with its reason in the word's entry).

decision: A lens has two faces: its glimpse takes data in, its showing gives it out. The glimpse says the data's place and relations and how it is entered with ease; so a lens defines the data it needs, and the shared language is no longer written from outside - its tables and relations become the glimpses of the lenses that need them, regrouped, not rewritten. ocoeco glimpse brings all lenses' glimpses together: subcommands and flags declared with argenv, a collision found when ocoeco is built; with no arguments it opens a composed view of them all. The acts are glimpse, observe and show; ocoeco note gives way to ocoeco glimpse. One lens defines a piece of data; other lenses may read it, safely, because lenses are additive.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the earlier concept of glimpses now has its place - a glimpse is a part of a lens; our database structure had been dictated by us from outside the system, and now fits in naturally; a glimpse also defines how to gather data with convenience - not retyping what already is, not dialling in what the computer can get; collisions are flagged in the making, never in use. It also answers a caution of the same day: a lens need not bring instruments of its own, because the entry follows from the declaration.
rejected: The shared language kept as one file apart from any lens; note as the way in (it asks one to know the tables); a glimpse for each table (a lens with several kinds of row has one glimpse with several entries); lenses loaded while running (a place builds its ocoeco with its lenses - the rhizoid way - so nothing is loaded blind).

decision: A projection is the shape that focusing gives the data: lines, a measure, how they sit together. It does not check what it projects - whether the data is sound is the data's (tad's rules, the relations), whether all of it was gathered is observing's - only the shape it is projected in. So the shape is told with no data at all: each part's query has its columns whether or not anything answers it, and a part's line and measure may name only those (ocoeco check asks the engine to describe each query over empty tables). A shape is checked in the making and need not be watched after; the world is checked where it is met, each time, in observing.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a projection does not check what it projects, it does not touch the data, it does not read text - it defines and self-checks the shape in which that data is projected; a shape like a progress bar, where we do not care what is in it; the shape that focusing gives data is a projection. This dissolves what was left open on 2026-11-12: what a lens expects of its own (at least one star, a total that equals a count) was asked of the wrong layer; and a part with no answers could not tell its line was wrong only because the shape was checked against a row of data. Proven: a misnamed column in a part with no answers, unseen before, is refused by its shape.
rejected: Expectations about data declared in a lens (another layer's work); checking the shape against the first answer (no answers, no check); watching the shape at every focus as the whole of awareness (a shape cannot change between making and running - the world can, and that is met in observing).

decision: A lens's glimpse is its entries, declared in the lens: what an entry is called, the table it fills, what a person is asked for, and what the computer supplies and when - new, always, FIELD changes, FIELD becomes VALUE. The computer knows today and who; what a person gives always stands. ocoeco glimpse alone shows every entry of every lens; ocoeco glimpse ENTRY --id ID --FIELD VALUE makes one, and a field the entry does not have is refused with what it does ask for. Two entries with one name, or an entry filling a table its lens does not define, stop the build. The work lens's first entry is item: since and driver are supplied.
why: Not to retype what already is, nor dial in what the computer can get (the author, 2026-11-12). Until now since and driver were typed by hand on every move, and ocoeco note took any field name, so a mistyped one was written as a new field.
rejected: A language of conditions (three plain ones cover the flow; more when a lens needs them); changing the shape of ocoeco glimpse "what was done" now (every job and every landing uses it: it goes on as before, and becomes an entry of the results lens when that lens gets its glimpse); flags built by argenv in this step (ocoeco's own command line is not on argenv yet: the collision is met at build all the same, by the build script).

decision: Every lens has its focus, and each brings what matters now rather than its whole tables: purpose - what each star is for and what is being reached; knowledge - what was looked into lately and the words with their meanings; reasoning - what was decided lately, what refines what, and how many decisions do not say what was rejected; results - what was done lately and what is still done by hand; looking back - the newest reflections and sessions. Each is three parts, a query and a line, and shows on every surface.
why: The fulldome said of five lenses that they had no focus yet. What was observed holds 95 milestones, 164 decisions, 142 glimpses, 173 sessions: laying all of it out would bring nothing into focus. What each lens is for comes from the research (the-fulldome-lens-by-lens).
rejected: Every row of every table (a list is not a focus); a focus for each table (a lens with four tables has one focus, as it has one glimpse); leaving the dotted lenses for later (the fulldome cannot stand where the engine's views do while five lenses show nothing).

decision: The shared language is held by the lenses that need it: the fourteen tables and thirteen relations moved from language.toml and relations.toml into six lens files (lenses/*.toml) - purpose, knowledge, reasoning, work, results, looking back - each saying what it is and which lens it grew from. ocoeco reads its language by putting the lenses' tables together. A lens id used twice, or a table defined by two lenses, stops ocoeco from building.
why: A lens defines the data it needs (2026-11-12-a-lens-has-a-glimpse); the structure was dictated from outside in one file. Regrouped, not rewritten: a test holds the lenses, put together, to the language as it stood, table for table and relation for relation. A collision is met in the making, never in use.
rejected: Keeping one file and tagging each table with a lens (the lens would still not own its data); checking collisions when ocoeco runs (met in use); rewriting any table while moving it (the proof would mean nothing).

decision: Reflection is an entity of the shared language (language.toml): id, date, by, over, saw, learned, changes, answers (other reflections) and touches (decisions, practices, backlog, research, glimpses - table:id in this project, project/table:id in another). Reflections are written into the data like everything else, so whoever comes next - a person or a machine - inherits the lessons, not only the state.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: reflect upon all that was done, as an entity related to the others. A session's lessons otherwise live in a conversation that ends; ocoeco is the place that lasts.
rejected: Keeping reflections in the session log (a log says what was done, in order; a reflection says what it meant, across a stretch); a reflection per project only (a look back often spans several, so it touches across projects); a separate field for each voice (each voice is its own reflection, and answers the other).

decision: The relations of the shared language are declared as data (relations.toml): which field refers to which table - twelve, among them two that were missing: a decision refining or replacing another (decisions.refines) and work serving a milestone or decision (backlog.serves). ocoeco check verifies every link within a star, and with --root the links into other stars. A field holds several links separated by commas or spaces; table:id names the table; project/table:id points into another star. A milestone's criteria are declared too; what in them is a condition rather than a link to a row (feature:name@level) is passed over.
why: The fulldome is one sky only if what is connected is truly connected (research the-fulldome-lens-by-lens, ocoeco-as-a-database): about 860 links were kept by discipline alone. On 2026-11-12 one decision refining another was written as prose eight times over.
rejected: Leaving relations to discipline; rewriting existing data to one separator (glimpses use spaces, reflections commas: both are read); putting the relations into tad's declaration now (tad's own references rule does not read lists or table:id yet - it should, later).

decision: What has run in each place is observed, not written: ocoeco observe (once harvest) gathers, for every place, the latest finished run of each active workflow on its default branch into the table runs, which the problems lens defines. A run that failed is a problem derived from the data - shown while true, gone when the next run passes - beside the problems people raise. The observatory observes, and so can the lab, with the same act; the lab will also say a new failure aloud.
why: On 2026-11-12 looking around found 111 runs failed on main in three days, three of them real and unheard for days (the phone docs' release 54 times; the harvest's guard 27). GitHub sends no notice that reaches anyone. The full picture must show it - a ping alone would be one more channel outside the picture.
rejected: A notification only, from each failing workflow (a sound without a light: nothing in the picture, and gone once read); raising each failure as a recorded problem (a fact of the data copied by hand, never closed when the run passes); polling from the lab alone (the picture is the observatory's, for everyone - the lab adds the voice).

decision: ocoeco's acts are record, observe and show. Observe replaces harvest and discover. Record stays plain. Show stays plain until the first lens is built and run; shine is kept in mind for it.
why: One word, one meaning; a word someone can guess from what it does (research the-words-for-the-acts).
rejected: pulse for record (taken by oco-agent's pulse, and it cannot be guessed); shine for show now (it reads as either of two acts); naming an act before touching it.

decision: The board is a view over every project's backlog (ocoeco board), never a list of its own. The backlog carries the flow - open, next, in-progress, waiting, parked, done, dropped - and four optional fields: driver (who holds it), next (its next step), since (the day it entered its state), waits_on. The board shows in progress by driver, waiting and on what, next, and what needs attention: more than three held by one driver, in progress with no next step or nobody holding it, nothing moved for a week. oco-agent speaks it when it changes. Refined the same day by 2026-11-12-the-room: the flow of work is one lens of the room, not the room.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the board must come from ocoeco's data, with ocoeco and oco-agent developed hand in hand, after the best research. One truth: the backlog is already kept in every project as the work goes; a second list is a second truth that drifts (lab-agent's board was one).
rejected: A board kept as its own list (lab-agent's board.json: a second truth); a column per project (the flow is the point, not where an item lives); priorities as numbers or points (the order is the next state, pulled; time is measured as age instead of estimated); hill charts now (worth adding once the flow is lived).

decision: The dome is the port and each surface an adapter: a lens brings its parts into focus (a heading and its lines), and a dome lays them out. Plain text and Markdown are surfaces behind that one port (ocoeco focus LENS --surface NAME), the terminal lays out through the text surface; HTML and CSS follow the same way. Lenses carry no layout of any surface: the two-space inset under a heading moved from the lenses' lines to the text surface.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: dome is the core term - the concept of a surface that stars' shine can be focused onto, the interface for surfaces to implement, be it Markdown, HTML and CSS, a terminal or whatever someone comes up with; and the fulldome is a lens that focuses all lenses onto all their surfaces. That is the canon's ports and adapters, reached from the picture. Proven: with the inset moved, both lenses and the board print byte for byte what they printed; and Markdown shows lenses that were written before it.
rejected: Surface as the core word (it names each made thing, not what they share); layout kept in a lens's lines (the text surface's inset had leaked into every lens); a surface for each lens (a lens would not just work on a surface made later).

decision: The view one can open and move in is the fulldome on one more surface: ocoeco fulldome opens every lens in the terminal - the lenses on the left, what the chosen one brings into focus on the right, g for what can be glimpsed through it - for this place or every place under a root. It is not a lens and no lens knows of it. What was lab-agent's board is a lens focusing; a terminal is one surface that lays a focus out, plain text another.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: what was a board is now just lenses focusing - the same shining of stars, through a lens, into focus, laid out into a terminal view. A lens says what comes into focus; where it is laid out is the surface. So the terminal needed no design of its own for each lens, and the work and problems lenses showed in it as they stood.
rejected: A lens for each surface (the same queries written again for every surface); a layout of its own for each lens in the terminal (a lens would stop just working on a surface made after it); a new name for the view (the fulldome is already the word for all lenses, touched not watched).

decision: The observatory's page shows the fulldome: after observing, ocoeco fulldome --observed data --surface html lays every lens out on the HTML and CSS surface, published beside the engine's site as fulldome.html. What was observed is a place a lens can focus on - a folder of tables whose every row names its project - so the acts follow each other as named: observe, then focus. The dome's port gains the fulldome: every lens together, each surface laying it out whole, and saying which lens brought nothing and why.
why: The engine's views are four thousand lines written by hand, one view at a time; a lens is declared once and shows on every surface. Publishing the fulldome beside them lets the two be compared before any view retires. Proven: the fulldome over the places on the lab's disk and over what the observatory observed show the same lines.
rejected: Replacing the engine's site at once (nothing to compare against, and five lenses have no focus yet); a second way of gathering for the page (what was observed is already a place); cloning every star in the observatory's builder (observing already brought their data).

decision: The problems lens is the andon: a problem is raised by whoever sees it - what, where, when, by whom - and stays in view until its countermeasure is written; writing the countermeasure is what handles it (the computer supplies the day). It also reads the work, to show what has stalled for more than a week. A lens may read tables other lenses define (reads); a read of a table no lens defines stops the build.
why: The largest gap the research found (research the-fulldome-lens-by-lens): on 2026-11-12, 21 release runs failed unseen and a watcher stayed silent for a night. At Toyota the cord is pulled by whoever sees a problem, and the light stays on until there is a countermeasure; nothing is closed by being marked closed.
rejected: Only derived problems (what a person notices has nowhere to go); only recorded ones (stalled work is already known from the data, and asking a person to copy it is the hand-work lenses end); a status to set by hand (a problem is handled when its countermeasure exists, so the countermeasure is what handles it); the hand-written check of what needs attention, kept apart (it is read here, from the same data).

decision: What a lens brings into focus, before any surface lays it out, is the projection: its parts, each line with what it is about and what it means. A projection looks at itself there, while it is still intelligible: each line has what it is about; the same thing is not shown twice in a part; a measure lies within its whole; a line names nothing its answers do not hold. What is not sound becomes a part of the projection itself - so every surface shows it, the voice says it and ocoeco check fails; never silently, and never as an exception no other program can use.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: what we have on different surfaces are results of projections, and while the data is intelligible in the form of a projection we can make a self check of what is being projected before it reaches the surface, not after it - as is often done in the world, resulting in an unmovable mess of regexes, text manipulations and reasonings in someone's head. On 2026-11-12 observed runs fed back into themselves, 45 shown as 135, and it was found by counting: this check finds it as it happens. Over every star, every place at once and what the observatory observed, every lens is sound.
rejected: Checking a surface's text (what was structure is by then a pot of text); a test beside the program, run once (the world changes after the test passes); stopping with an error when not sound (the rest of the picture would vanish with it, and nothing could be done with the error); mending silently.

decision: What is worth saying is what newly came into view. Each line a lens brings into focus knows what it is about - its star and id when the answer names them - so ocoeco focus LENS --since FILE says only what is new in a headed part since last time, and what is no longer in view at all, keeping the focus for next time. A total is not news, nor a line whose words changed (an age) about the same thing; the first time only keeps. It works for any lens and over what was observed (--observed).
why: lab-agent's daemon pushed the whole board to the author's phone every few minutes; in OCO's shape the board is a lens, and a person needs what changed - an item taken up, a problem raised or handled - not the whole again. Built once for every lens rather than for the board.
rejected: The whole board said again each time (noise that hides the change); comparing lines as text (every age and count would be news every day); a mechanism for the board alone (the problems lens needs the same).

decision: A part of a projection has a shape, and a chain is one: a lens says a part is a chain - from this value to that - and every surface walks it from where it begins, a line and then the lines that go on from where it arrives, each once, whatever order the rows were kept in. How far along looks is the surface's own: set in on text and on a screen, nested in Markdown, moved over on a page. And a line keeps its named values in the projection, not only its words - so a surface, a program or an agent reads what a line is made of (--surface json).
why: The red line of the route was first laid out as a list sorted by name: the connections were true and the order of the route was gone. The author had asked that it be seen that from x followed y, z and d, and from them g; and that an agent use the projection, before the pot, as its interface - which a line glued to text could not be. Setting aside lines that keep their values as a game of looks was wrong: it is what a chain and an agent both stand on. Lists are unchanged: four lenses print byte for byte what they printed.
rejected: Ordering the rows in the query (the order of a walk is not an order of rows: one row may be reached two ways); a chain drawn by one surface (the next surface would not have it); a lens that sets its own indentation (looks in a lens).

decision: A lens can be entered like anything else, and kept by a place as rows: the lens of language takes a lens (what it says of itself, what it reads) and its parts (what each asks and how a line is laid out - or which lens it places, and under which heading). A place that keeps such rows has that lens: it is in view wherever the place is, held to what every lens is held to, and seen by the lens of language like any other. The rows carry a lens whole in what it says and what it brings into focus - every lens built into ocoeco, turned into rows and back, is the lens it was. A lens's own tables and entries are not yet carried by rows.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: we need a lens that shapes data so that a lens is the outcome - lenses defined as data - a lens that makes lenses. The lens of language could read lenses as rows and not make one; its own line said language - takes no entry. And the rows described a lens without being one: a part's row did not say whether it is always shown, its measure, its chain, or what it is laid out per.
rejected: Rows that describe a lens and are not it (two forms that can disagree); a way of entering lenses apart from entries (a lens is entered like anything else); carrying a lens's own tables and entries by rows before the trial has shown what that asks (left, and said).

decision: A part of a lens may be what another lens brings into focus, placed there - all of it, or the part under one heading. It asks nothing itself: the other lens gathers, shapes and lays out. A lens made of such parts is a lens of lenses: a named arrangement that says only what to place together. Lenses placed in a ring are said, not followed. The work lens places the part of the lens of signs for what has not moved, and no longer asks the same.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a lens of lenses does not care about the data that passes its shapes - where to get it, how to shape it and project it is done by those lenses; it shapes only which shapes to place together, and a sheet so made can itself be made into a word. It answered what could not be seen the day before - how a projection feeds another lens: by being placed. And it met a sign showing since that afternoon: the lens of language showed that signs and work each asked, in their own words, what has not moved for more than seven days, and there was no way for one lens to show another's part. The fulldome is such a lens with its arrangement written in code.
rejected: The same query kept in two lenses (one changed, the other disagrees); a lens reading another lens's rows after they are laid out (the shape is intelligible before any surface); a new kind of thing for an arrangement (it is a lens).

decision: A milestone is reached when what it rests on is done, and that is read off the work, never typed: the purpose lens counts, for each milestone, how many of the backlog items its criteria name are done - a measure whose whole is the line's own (a measure may take its whole from the answer: whole = COLUMN). Criteria that are conditions told by tests are not judged by this lens, and it says how many. readiness is shown as what it is - a milestone's rung on the path, earned in order - not as how ready it is.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a milestone is praise of a great work done, or of a great work ahead that fills a gap, merges overlaps or clarifies the whole; so far they were placed from our heads, out of taste - and the tool should show them, as intelligible data from intelligible data. Looking up what readiness meant found it had been misread for days: it is the rung (1 to 9; the specification: readiness is earned in order along the path), not a share done. The lens had drawn a rung as a filled bar, and a problem had been raised against Rhizoid for a milestone at 9 that was simply the ninth rung, rightly not reached.
rejected: The rung drawn as a measure (a number shown as progress that is not progress); a share of readiness typed by hand (taste, not evidence); judging here what tests tell (the engine does, from the phone's own data; this lens says it does not).

decision: A place may bring its own lenses: lens files kept beside its mark, in lenses/, read as the program runs. They are found wherever that place is in view - by focus, the fulldome, the check - beside the lenses built into ocoeco, and held to what the build holds those to, said when they are looked through: no id used twice, no table defined by two lenses; one lens brought by several places is one lens. A lens a place keeps under a built-in one's id is that lens's own text - the built-in one is looked through, and the check says when the two no longer agree.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: what lenses do is left behind the brackets of an interface, in Rust code. Tried the same day with the lab's own record: oco-agent keeps a journal and beats in the language a lens declares tables in, and nothing could read them, because the set of lenses was whatever ocoeco was built with. Marked as a place bringing a lens made of its own declaration, what is being done now came into focus - to the minute, typed by nobody; the job that tried it saw itself.
rejected: The lab's tables written into ocoeco's own lenses (ocoeco would know oco-agent); a lens that cannot be looked through until ocoeco is rebuilt (behind the brackets); a brought lens free of what built-in ones are held to (a table defined twice, met in use).

decision: The mark says what place this is beyond a star, and what it gathers: [place] is = constellation or observatory, gathers = stars as owner/repository or every star of an owner as owner/*. A mark that says nothing of it is a star's. So a star may be gathered by many places, and a place may gather a star that lives elsewhere. What a star is for - its kind - is another question and stays as it is. Standing in a place that gathers, ocoeco fulldome and focus show what it gathers: the same at every scale, with no flag. The four stars of kind lens, in the old sense, are the constellations: each already named its family in lens.toml, and ocoeco check holds the mark and that file in agreement while the file lives.
why: Everything else speaks of places, lenses and acts; the mark still said only kind and parent - nineteen of twenty-two stars with one parent, a flat list where there is a sky. Deferred on 2026-11-12 until the first lenses; there are seven, on four surfaces. Looking before replacing found that what a constellation gathers was already written down: lens.toml's family, owners and projects - many to many, as parent could not be.
rejected: A new list beside lens.toml with nothing holding them together (they would drift); deriving the place from lens.toml alone (the mark would still not say what a place is, and that file is the old engine's); replacing kind (it answers another question); removing parent now (the engine's views still read it: it goes when they retire).

decision: A surface has two directions: it lays a projection out, and it reads back what someone gives there. A line typed in a shell is such a surface, and its reading back is argenv's own reader, as it is: what an entry may be given is handed to it as records made while the program runs - a field is an input, its allowed values the input's - and what was typed comes back as what was given, or as what could not be taken, said in the entry's words. ocoeco's own reading of typed words is retired. What an entry means stays with the lens: whether it is new or a change, what the computer supplies, which rows a field may point at.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: argenv is basically another lens - with the terminal as the surface it projects onto. Looked at against our own words it comes apart into two things already had: its declaration is what every lens carries, what can be entered; its reader, help and completions are the terminal as a surface - in the direction our surfaces lacked. One setting with two doors is one field coming back through two surfaces. Tried first with a throwaway program, then made: a misspelt field is answered with what was meant and a value outside a field's set is refused with the set, neither of which ocoeco's own reader did.
rejected: A second way of declaring what can be entered, for the reader's sake (the lens already declares it); a build step making the reader's declarations (records are made as the program runs); keeping ocoeco's own reader beside argenv's (one nature, twice).

decision: An observatory is where one looks from: standing in one, what the machine itself holds is in view - the places its programs keep of themselves, found where programs keep their own data. They are not gathered, are named in no mark, and do not leave the machine; what is in view says so in words. A constellation shows what it gathers and no more.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: running continuously, it can treat its surroundings as part of the flow. oco-agent's record became a place bringing the lens of now, and was seen only by standing in its own folder: the author's observatory gathers what is discovered on GitHub, and the record is not there - nor should what the lab does be published. Where a thing lives and who can reach it from where: from where one looks, what is there is in view.
rejected: Pushing the lab's record somewhere to be gathered (it is the lab's own, and the jobs it names are private); naming the machine in the observatory's mark (a public mark; and every other machine looked from would need its line); a link among the projects (someone would have to make it, and remember to).

decision: A place observes what its mark says it gathers, and itself - not whatever is found on a platform. constellation is a kind, for a place that is for nothing but gathering. ocoeco init --gathers writes what a place gathers into its mark from its first day, and refuses it for a star. A place whose mark names nothing gathered - the first observatory - observes all that is found, as before.
why: OCO is the ecosystem, not an observatory (2026-11-12-many-observatories): anyone may have one. Until now observing took every marked repository on GitHub - all of them the author's, so it showed nothing; the day another person marks one, an observatory would gather theirs unasked. The author's own observatory is next, in its own organization, tracking OCO as one constellation among his.
rejected: Observing everything and filtering when showing (what was never asked for would still be fetched and kept); a list of places kept apart from the mark; making the first observatory name its stars now (it is untouched until its replacement stands).

decision: A connection is a row: this - how - that, with one line of why and how it is known (recorded, measured, read or reasoned), and the red line it belongs to. It runs between two particular rows of any tables, in any stars. Four kinds to begin with: led to, needed, halted, repeats. The lens of insight defines it, with an entry to draw one and a focus that lays each red line out. A reflection is what a red line is summed up in; it is not a second kind of prose. The projection itself is a surface (--surface json): its parts as structure, for a program or an agent to read before any pot.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: knowledge is kept as if it had value in itself, and research as dead gathering of facts, without their other side - insight: seeing connections where they were not seen, where things overlap, where there are gaps, how the whole fits together. A story written as prose is a pot that lost the relations it had one step before: that from x followed y, z and d, and from them g; what was a necessity, for what and of what kind; what was halted while it lacked. The retrospective of the same day had found that necessity has no link, and carried its chain in sentences.
rejected: More relations declared on tables (a relation is for a whole table; a connection is found between two rows no schema foresaw); tables of their own for summaries, insights and stories (reflections already hold what was seen, learned and what it changes - they lacked something to stand on); a connection without how it is known (a reasoned red line must look reasoned, or the tidy story returns); a terminal as the only way in (reading the whole through it costs even an agent).

decision: A person makes an entry from the fulldome: on any lens, e opens a form for that lens's entries - the declaration ocoeco glimpse reads, described once. It asks only what a person is asked for; a field with set values is chosen with the arrows, not typed; what the computer supplies is shown as supplied; giving the id of a row that exists changes that row; a lens with several entries offers each. It is written the way every row is - guarded: one that would add a link to nowhere is refused, the reason shown in the form and what was typed kept. An entry is made only where one place is stood in, so it has somewhere to go.
why: The route, looked back over on 2026-11-13: lab-agent began as hands for a driver who had none, and gave the author a box to answer in on 10 November; the lenses that replaced its board could only be read - the one thing taken away and not given back. It halts the old daemon's retiring, and it is the first need of the route come round again (connections no-hands-no-switch and hands-again, in OCO's place).
rejected: A form written by hand for each entry (the entry is already declared: fields, needed ones, set values, what is supplied); typing a status (a set value mistyped is a refusal that need not happen); writing from where many places are in view (the row would have no place of its own); a way of writing apart from the guarded one.

decision: ocoeco is released the way tad is: release-please keeps a release pull request open from the commits; merging it tags ocoeco-vX.Y.Z; and the package conveyor - called, not copied - builds the files for each kind of machine in the same run: a tarball, a .deb and an .rpm for x86_64 and aarch64, with their checksums and signed provenance. ocoeco keeps only what is its own: its declaration for the conveyor and its two build scripts. The first release is the first version that was ever released; 0.1.0 never was.
why: Until now ocoeco existed only as built from main on the lab: the tool at the centre of the commons could be on one machine, and a lens added there could be looked through nowhere else. The driver who works on the commons most looked at it for days by asking the lab to look. Tried the same day: handed the lab's own build privately, the driver elsewhere asked, waited and looked with the commons' own programs at once - but on a favour, and already one landing behind.
rejected: A release path of ocoeco's own (tad's exists, and the conveyor is where everything around a build lives, once); handing builds over by hand (it worked as a trial, and rests on someone remembering); waiting for a first stable version to release (it is used daily, and changes daily).

decision: A row moves from one place to another with every link kept true: ocoeco move TABLE ID... --to PLACE rewrites each link to it - in the place it leaves, in the place it comes to, and with --root in every place held here - to where it now is, and its own links to what stays behind say which place that is. If anything would then point nowhere, nothing is moved and every file is as it was.
why: Places are being told apart - OCO a constellation, the author's observatory his own - and what was recorded in whichever star one stood in must find its home. A row is not only its line: nine later decisions refine the ones about the whole, words name them, reflections touch them. Moved by hand, each of those links would point nowhere. The first observatory's own records will need the same when it retires.
rejected: Copying rows and leaving the old ones (two truths); moving by hand and mending what the check then finds (the links break first, and only the ones the check knows are found); refusing to move anything that is pointed at (nothing about the whole could then move).

decision: Text has two surfaces. Text that flows: continuous lines, wrapped as whatever shows them likes - it requires nothing and promises nothing of how it looks. And the screen: text as a volume of so many columns of monospaced characters, unwrapped (ocoeco focus or fulldome --surface screen --width N). Into it each shape is fitted by its own rule - a line's continuation sits under where it began, a bar is never broken, a word wider than a line is broken where the line ends - so no line reaches past the width, whatever the data. A surface says what it requires of whatever shows it, so that when it looks wrong it can be said why; and the screen looks at its own shape before a character is written, saying in itself if a line reaches past.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: when we constrain the volume - by how many monospaced characters fit in a line - text becomes a screen, and the shapes in a projection are tied to the surface they are projected onto; if an editor wraps or is not monospaced that is not the projection's concern - its concern is that these shapes, projected this way, give exactly this shape, and it can say exactly why it looks wrong: it defined the shape, the constraints, the borders, how the shapes lie together. Like a puzzle: the whole shape is defined first and the pieces carved in it, so they are guaranteed to come together. The bar of ten cells had assumed monospace without saying so; the terminal surface already carved one rectangle into others, and was tested at a stated volume both times. Proven over what was observed: at 100, 72 and 48 columns nothing reaches past the width, and the words are those of the flowing text, in the same order.
rejected: One text surface that guesses a width (the requirement stays unsaid); cutting what does not fit (data lost to make a shape); leaving a too-long word to reach past (the guarantee would hold only for kind data); the terminal's library for plain text (a screen written to a file needs no terminal).

decision: A lens can be looked at as its beam: not what it brings into focus, but how light travels through it - what enters (each table it gathers, how many rows, from how many places); what each part lets pass (what it asks of, rows in and answers through, shown as how much of the light passes - or which lens it places, and how much of that comes through); and where it goes on to (the lenses that place it, the surfaces it is laid out on). It is a projection like any other: ocoeco focus LENS --beam, and in the fulldome b turns the lens in view into its beam and back.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a lens of lenses that shows the relations of lenses, not the shapes they project - a line where information enters a lens, the lens's name, how its focus cuts off parts of the data, a line that continues into other lenses or down to a surface; and changing, a click away, between a projection and the beam it came by - so that everything is transparent, and the making of it too.
rejected: A drawing of every lens at once (the beam of one lens is what can be read off and checked; the whole drawn later, from the same rows); counting what is cut off as rows in minus answers (a count that gathers is not a cut; how much passes is said as a measure); a view written apart from the surfaces (it is a projection, laid out by any).

decision: What is in progress on the board is read off the work, and no longer typed: an item that a record of work advanced lately, and that is not said to be done, is in progress - by whom, how often, when last, with its next step; one said to be done is finished lately. It is one question, laid out once for each. What is left for a person to say is intent: this is next, this is done, this is set aside. An item typed in progress that no work advances is shown as that - a sign, until the typed state is no longer set by anyone.
why: Decided that morning (states are read off the act) with the typed states left standing until the read-off ones had earned trust. In one day the typed board drifted twice under the hand that kept it, each time found only by reading it back to the author: three items in progress whose steps were done or halted; an item marked next that had been finished for hours. The seeing was already there, one part below the part that drifted. The author: correcting by hand a thing we decided should not be set by hand is itself a sign of a gap, and a gap is filled by clearer seeing, not by more handwork.
rejected: Keeping the typed state as the headline (it drifted twice in a day); setting the state from the act when work is recorded (a state still stored, and able to go stale); two queries for in progress and finished (the same question, written twice - the lens of language would say so).

decision: The lenses themselves are rows, and a lens looks at them: the lens of language. Each lens in view - built into ocoeco or brought by a place - is read as data: the lens, each table it defines, each field, each entry it takes, each part it brings into focus, every row saying where its lens is kept. No place keeps these tables: ocoeco fills them from the lenses as they are, and a test holds what the lens declares equal to what the rows carry. What it brings into focus are signs, shown while true: a field declared again and again, the same line of a query written more than once, a table nothing brings into focus, a lens that takes nothing or brings nothing into focus. It shows; whoever sees merges - nothing here changes a lens.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: ocoeco looking at itself with its ecosystem can clarify itself, see what overlaps, which lenses handle the same nature and how they merge - healing, as against an unintelligible growth of lenses. Tried by hand first, with a search and guesses at how a query is spelled: half the counts came back broken or contradicting themselves. The lenses were the one thing in the commons still kept only as text a program reads - the language that makes everything else intelligible was not intelligible to itself.
rejected: Counting the lenses' text with a search (it failed when tried); the lenses written out as files a place keeps (they would drift from the lenses, and need a step to remember); a tool that merges what overlaps by itself (it would hide what the lens shows).

decision: The lens of problems is the lens of signs. A sign is said by whoever sees it: what, where, and what kind - stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear. It is shown while nothing has come of it, and stops being shown when a connection leads from it to what was seen; nothing is asked about what was done. Many signs may lead to one thing, and then stop together. No table is added: what bears on what is a connection. The table keeps the name it was stored under, and rows written before are as they were written.
why: Decided on 2026-11-13 (what does not fit is a sign) and not done: for two days the lens went on saying countermeasure on every line, read past until it was shown to the author. Laid side by side from the data before reshaping: that one thing needs another is written five ways - an item serves, a milestone rests on, a connection, an item waits on, a countermeasure - and the last two are sentences nothing can follow: of eleven waits, one names a row; of seventeen countermeasures, none. A table of needs was about to be designed; a connection already is one.
rejected: A table of needs (a sixth way of saying it); a field for what was done, as a link (a connection is that, and can be drawn from anywhere); renaming the stored table and its fields (rows in eight places rewritten for a name - a name is not the place it names).

decision: A projection is the topmost shape of shapes, and it is cut from the whole: fulldome, lens, part, line, place - each a shape taken from the one above. That each piece has exactly one place is guaranteed by its having been cut from there, not by rules about what a piece must be. A lens's line is such a cut: it divides a line into places, so what fills one can never land in another. A projection comes hand in hand with what it is projected onto, as a port with its adapters.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: this guarantee does not come from a set of rules. A puzzle starts as a whole; anyone can make one by cutting a picture into pieces, with no rules of what the individual shapes must be - the pieces are guaranteed to make the whole and their places are fixed, because it was a whole and each piece had exactly one place. Projection is just the topmost shape of shapes. This settles what was left open on 2026-11-13 (which of two nested shapes the word names): there are not two things.
rejected: A guarantee from rules for each piece (joints) - the direction was backwards; two words for the shape of the data and the shape fitted to a volume (one whole, cut); checking after writing that nothing reaches past the width (a whole cut rightly cannot; a volume too small is a cut that cannot be made, and belongs at the cutting).

decision: A field's place in the order of its table is its ordinal, not at: at holds a moment everywhere else. Every built-in lens's rows and the rows OCO's place keeps say it so.
why: The lens of language's sharper question, asked the first time: at held integers in beats, journal and said (moments, in seconds), strings in glimpses and runs (moments, as text), and in lens_fields a place in order - named so that same day.
rejected: position (a word the query language keeps for itself); seat, nth (less plain).

decision: Within one look a lens is brought into focus once: a lens that places parts of another is given the same bringing each time. What was brought is not kept beyond the look.
why: Sign a-look-is-slower-than-is-understood. Timed lens by lens on 2026-11-14: the author's sheet took 4.7 s where the lens of signs took 0.9 - it places three parts of signs, two of work, one of purpose, and each placed part brought the whole placed lens into focus anew. The same nature as the graph made twice, one level up; and it was found by measuring, after a prediction made without measuring had been off by a factor of three.
rejected: Placing a part without bringing its lens (a part may ask of shapes its lens names; the lens is what is brought).

decision: A lens can be looked through from a thing - lens@thing - as an observatory is looked from somewhere: wherever the lens says {here}, the thing stood on. The lens of around does so: from one thing, what it points at and what points at it, each by how, with a few words of what each is; to step is to stand on a neighbour. What fits offers the things to stand on - the kind first, then the thing. Every thing in the graph says what it is in a few words. And the lens of the graph measures how far the work can be walked up: from a record of work to an item, to what the item serves, to a milestone that rests on it.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: what is most important is not the structure alone but navigating in it - between composition, concrete work answering concrete needs, and decomposition, moving back to see the plane one is on from the plane before - without losing the relations that were there in the details. Looked at first: no lens looked from one thing; each looked across a kind. And of 309 records of work, 198 reached an item, 93 what that item serves, 37 a milestone - relations thin out going up.
rejected: A view of its own for walking (it is a lens, laid out by any surface, offered by what fits); naming the thing only in full (a star names its place where there is one of that name); directions - up, down - declared on relations before use has shown which way each points.

decision: A lens is kept by a place as rows, whole: what it says and reads, its tables with their fields in order, its relations, its entries with what the computer supplies, and its parts. The lens of language takes an entry for each - lens, table, field, entry, relation, part - and an entry is found among the lenses in view from the place it is entered in, built in or brought. So a place can make a new kind of data through entries alone, enter into it through the entry it made, and look through the lens it made; every lens built into ocoeco, as rows and back, is the lens it was.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: a lens that shapes data so that a lens is the outcome - lenses defined as data. A lens could be kept as rows since that day, but only one that places or asks: the rows did not carry a lens's tables, relations or entries, so a lens kept as rows could not define anything. Tried in a throwaway place: a lens of questions made through entries alone, a question entered through the entry it made, and seen through it.
rejected: A table's declaration kept as one block of text in a row (the language would hold a piece of itself it cannot read); entries found only among the lenses built in (a lens a place makes could not be entered into); a place's tables added to its mark by an entry in the same step (what a place keeps is the place's own word).

decision: A place may say other names its tables are known by, in its mark: a name, and the table it names. A link written with any of them holds, and the graph names the row by the table's own name. And a relation may say that a link carries a level after a mark: a condition a milestone rests on (feature:voice-calls@linux-best, component:kernel@xiaomi-surya) is a link whose row is the feature or component and whose level is what follows @; one over every feature, or over no kind of row (tests@a-device), names no row and is not a link. The phone's docs say that feature and component are other names for features and components. So conditions are edges like any link: checked, walked, counted.
why: Sign a-condition-names-its-table-otherwise: 45 conditions were passed over, and the graph said nothing pointed at any feature while conditions did. The author: a name is not the place it names; many names may point at one place. Tried in a copy before anything landed: the first trial found conditions of three kinds - feature, component, and tests at a device - and stopped; set right, none pointed nowhere.
rejected: Guessing a plural; rewriting the conditions another program reads; changing the relation that passes conditions over (the language grows: a second relation says what the first did not, and the first stands as it stood); a list of exceptions for what is not a link (a level said of no kind of row names no row).

decision: The lens of language asks which names hold different kinds of thing in different tables, where it listed every field declared more than twice: a name used again for the same kind is one word used rightly (id in every table); a name that holds a date string in one table and a number in another is where names collide.
why: Looked through on 2026-11-14: the list said 16 fields were declared again and again, id first, in 26 tables - mostly the same word used rightly; it could not tell a shared word from a collision, and so said nothing anyone could act on.
rejected: Keeping both parts (the old one is the new one's noise); declaring each field once as a word shared by every table (a restructuring the look did not ask for).

decision: A part may name the shape it makes, and the other parts of the lens ask of it by that name, as of a table: the shapes a lens names are made ready in order before its parts are asked - when it is brought into focus, in its beam, and when its shape is checked. A named shape with no line of its own is not laid out: it is passed on through. Its name may not be a table's. The beam shows it as what it shapes, and the parts that ask of it as taking their light from it. Purpose shapes what each milestone rests on once, as rests, and both its parts ask of it.
why: Met from the side of the data (sign one-shape-asked-twice-in-purpose): what each milestone rests on was asked twice in the same words, and before that twice in words just different enough that the lens of language could not see it - because a part could not name a shape for another to ask of. It is the author's projection that feeds another lens, in its smallest form: within one lens.
rejected: A shape kept in a place as a table (it would drift from what it shapes); asking a shape across lenses in the same step (within one lens first, where what it asks is plain); a shape laid out as well whether or not it has a line (a shape is light passed on, not a picture).

decision: A row entered through an entry is remembered as what the next record of work touched, as a row written by note is: a record of work says all it changed. And the work lens shows a next step said before the work that followed it - work recorded on an item after its next step was last said. Where it is not known when a step was last said, nothing is shown.
why: Sign a-next-step-typed-goes-stale. Looked at, 2026-11-14: only 12 of 332 items say a next step, and of 7 with work done after, five named a step already taken - the simplest lens a trial made that morning, read-off-the-act a step done two days before. And it could not yet be read off soundly: every one said last said, never - a record of work noted what it changed only for rows written with one command, not through entries, by which nearly everything is written.
rejected: Dropping the next step (an intention is a person's to say); showing every step whose saying is not known as stale (not known is not stale); a date typed beside each step (another state to keep true).

decision: The part of the work lens showing a next step said before the work that followed it is taken back. Whether a step has been taken cannot be read off work recorded after it was said: working toward a step is not the step done. What stands of the day's change: a row entered through an entry is remembered as what the next record of work touched.
why: Within the hour it showed a step as passed that was exactly right: a route is a lens had its next step said at 19:39, and minutes later a record of work was made standing on it - a sign being entered - and the part showed it. It could not tell work toward a step from the step being done, and so showed on ordinary work.
rejected: A number of records after which a step counts as passed (a rule in place of seeing); keeping it on the sheet as a prompt to look (the sheet is for what shows, not for what might). What would read it off: a next step that is a link to what is to be done, as waiting became a link to what halts - a change to what a next step is, not a query.

decision: Observing a part - only what has run - writes only that part's tables: the places found and what a whole observation found wrong are left as the whole observation wrote them.
why: Tried before one observer of runs was made of the author's observatory: observing only what has run into its data rewrote the places found and what the observation found wrong - the second to nothing - so a look at a part would have erased what a look at the whole had found.
rejected: Merging what a part found wrong into what the whole found (which a part did not look at, it cannot say is gone).

decision: A projection is a plane, and a plane can hold planes. A lens placed whole is placed as its plane - its name, what it says, its own shapes - kept within the placing lens; one part of a lens placed is that shape among the placing lens's own. Every surface lays out a plane, planes within it included, the one way it knows; what is the surface's own is only its frame - a title, and for a page its style. The fulldome is a lens like any other: it places every lens in view, each keeping its own shape - so the fulldome's own kind, and each surface's second way of laying it out, are gone. Lenses stacked read a shape before any surface (a named shape, read across lenses); lenses side by side are placed in a plane. Every surface lays the fulldome out as before, line for line, but that the language now counts it as a lens.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: what we call a projection is a plane - all shapes of shapes in one plane - much easier to feed into another plane of lenses before it hits a surface, where the shape of the data is lost; a lens that places lenses side by side is a plane-lens (instances such as a fulldome of some stars), and lenses stacked one after another read the preceding plane and leave out what their focus does not pass. Looked at first: the plane was flat - placing a lens poured its parts into the placing lens, nothing keeping them together - so the fulldome had a kind of its own, and five surfaces each a second way of laying it out, 77 lines written because a plane could not hold a plane.
rejected: Keeping the fulldome as its own kind beside lenses (a plane-lens written in code); flattening a placed lens (its shape of shapes lost); a lens reading another lens's lines as laid out (light bounced off a surface - stacking reads the shape before it).

decision: The graph follows the relations of every lens in view - those built into the program, and those a place brings: a relation is a relation whoever declares it.
why: The conversation, made a place on 2026-11-14 with its lens entered through entries: each of 2,881 turns says which it follows, the place's lens declares that relation - and the graph had none of those links, for it read relations only from the lenses built in. Standing on a turn showed nothing. The author: adjust ocoeco itself with how it can express all that, fit in the whole, discover itself in it.
rejected: Declaring the conversation's relation in the program (the program would have to know of every place's kinds); leaving a place's relations to its own lens's queries (a link is a link in the one graph, or it cannot be walked).

decision: A lens may say a route: a table whose rows are not kept by a place but read from a kind of surface, where each place in view is held, when they are asked for - stored nowhere. A route is part of the language like a relation or an entry: a row, entered through an entry, shown by the lens of language. The kinds of surface are few, each a small adapter in the program; the first is git history - each change to a place's repository, its name, when, by whom, what it says of itself. What the lenses in view keep out is kept out of what a route reads, as it is read. The beam says from which surface the rows were read, and when.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: a lens takes the shape of data from a surface and lays it on another; the lens behind does not care where the shape came from; what is called a place is how to get to it and what it has, and the lenses themselves show how to get there. Looked at then: five ways in, all written in the program, and of ten surfaces not yet read most lacked one thing - a route. Others who read a surface as a table (research reading-a-surface-as-a-table) say the shape as data, keep the kinds of surface as a few adapters, and say beside the shape which surface is read. Tried: a place made a lens with a route through entries alone - no Rust, no file edited - and looked through its own history.
rejected: A route that runs what it is told to (a lens takes a shape from what is; it does not act); rows read from a surface copied into a file of the place (a second copy, as of some moment nobody says); the history read by the program for every place whether or not a lens asks (what is read is said by a lens, or it is not seen to be read).

decision: How a place is got to is a route, and a route says as of when: a folder with a mark is held here, as it is now; what an observatory observed is as of when it observed; what the machine keeps is as of when it was last written; what the program makes from the lenses or the links is made now. A lens's beam says of each table by which route its rows came, and as of when.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: what is called a place is not so much something fixed - it is how to get to it and how to get what it has; lenses can do that, and themselves show how to get there. Looked at first: the program has five ways in, and three of them said nothing of as of when - yet routes differ in exactly that, and showing what was observed as if it were so now is how the false alarms about failing runs began.
rejected: A place taken to be its route (the same place reached two ways would be two places: a place is what its mark says it is, the same along every route); the routes rebuilt as lenses in one step (looked at and said first; what the beam shows decides what follows).

decision: A row written is held to its table's declaration as the place speaks the language: the lenses built into ocoeco, and the lenses the place brings - as files or kept as rows. A table a place's own lens defines is checked as any other; a value is written as the kind its field declares.
why: Sign a-row-is-checked-only-against-the-built-in-lenses: only the built-in lenses were the declaration a row is held to, so a lens made through entries would have taken any word for any field.
rejected: A declaration made once for every place (each place speaks the language with its own lenses too); a place's lenses free of the declaration (a lens that defines a table says what its rows are).

decision: A route may say which of what its surface holds, and the shape carved from each. Of the kind files: which names the paths within the place - any folders, any name - and where no shape is said each file is a row; where one is, every place in a file the shape is found is a row, what the shape names being its fields, with the path and the line. A place reads its own files. So the source a place holds and the guards written for it are two routes of one kind, said in the language - the lens of the program - and not an adapter each.
